summary: Pi 0.85.1's extension surface offers no subagent/spawn API and no model-call API of its own: extensions get `ctx.modelRegistry` (a synchronous compat facade over ModelRuntime with `complete`/`streamSimple`) plus `pi.exec` and raw `node:child_process`. The only subagent mechanism the SDK documents/implements is an example extension that spawns a separate `pi --mode json -p --no-session` child process. There is no documented or implemented concurrency limit/queue/rate-limiter for model requests: `ModelRegistry.complete` is a thin passthrough to `ModelRuntime.complete` → `provider.stream(...).result()`, with retry/timeout settings only. Bounded parallelism must therefore be implemented by the extension itself (Scholar already does this: `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6` worker pool in review-layer.ts with abortable calls against `ctx.modelRegistry.complete`/`provider.streamSimple`).

files.description: ExtensionAPI (line 906) and ExtensionContext (line 209) declarations — the complete answer to Q1/Q5. No spawn/subagent member; `exec` at 993, `registerTool` at 944, `events: EventBus` at 1083, `signal`/`abort`/`isIdle` at 236-240, `modelRegistry` at 221.
ModelRegistry is the only model-call path an extension gets via ctx.modelRegistry; `complete` delegates to ModelRuntime (model-registry.js:65-66).
ModelRuntime.stream/complete implementation (458-460) — no limiter, queue, or semaphore anywhere on the model-request path (Q3).
Extension load model: jiti `moduleCache: false` (417), per-(cwd) factory cache (409-414), factory re-invoked per load (458-462) — grounds Q4 on module-state sharing.
The only sanctioned subagent pattern: registerTool("subagent") that spawns a separate `pi` process (300, 346) with Promise.all worker fan-out (235).

Existing Scholar code that already calls ctx.modelRegistry.complete / provider.streamSimple with signal and runs a bounded worker pool (REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6, review-layer.ts:76,513) — the surface a plan must build on.

architecture: Layering (all confirmed by reading dist/*.d.ts + the matching .js next to them): ExtensionAPI/ExtensionContext (dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts) ← ExtensionRunner (runner.d.ts, `createContext()` at runtime) ← per-process extension loader (loader.js, jiti-based, module instance cached per path+cwd) ← coding agent session (core/sdk.ts `createAgentSession`, AgentSessionRuntime). Model calls an extension can make go: ctx.modelRegistry.complete → ModelRuntime.complete → ModelRuntime.stream → provider.stream(...).result() (bundled pi-ai at node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/models.js:387-399 for the Models class, model-runtime.js:458-460 for the coding-agent wrapper). Subagent work is NOT part of the SDK: the shipped example spawns a fresh `pi` OS process. Abort plumbing is `ctx.signal` (signal: AbortSignal | undefined) injected into every tool `execute(..., signal, ...)` and available on turn-scoped contexts.
report:
# Findings — pi 0.85.1 extension capabilities (SDK root: `C:/Users/basam/AppData/Local/pi-node/current/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)

## 1. What `ExtensionAPI` exposes

Full interface: `dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:906` → `1084`.
```ts
export interface ExtensionAPI {
    on(event: "project_trust", handler: ProjectTrustHandler): void;   // 907
export interface ExtensionAPI {                                        // 906
    /** Shared event bus for extension communication. */
    events: EventBus;                                                  // 1082-1083
```

**(a) spawn a subagent / task — NONE.** No member named `spawn*`, `task`, `agent(s)`, `runTask`, `createSession*`. The only process/command entry point is:
```ts
    /** Execute a shell command. */
    exec(command: string, args: string[], options?: ExecOptions): Promise<ExecResult>;   // types.d.ts:992-993
```
with `ExecOptions = { signal?: AbortSignal; timeout?: number; cwd?: string }` (`dist/core/exec.d.ts:8-14`). Everything else process-related is raw `node:child_process` imported by the extension itself (as the example does, `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:15` → `import { spawn } from "node:child_process";`). Session lifecycle members exist only on `ExtensionCommandContext` (`newSession`/`fork`/`switchSession`/`navigateTree`, types.d.ts:264-293) or on `ReplacedSessionContext` (`sendMessage`/`sendUserMessage`, types.d.ts:297-305) — they replace *the current* session, they do not create parallel workers.

**(b) invoke a tool — no direct invocation API.** There is registration and tool-name bookkeeping only:
```ts
    /** Register a tool that the LLM can call. */
    registerTool<TParams extends TSchema = TSchema, TDetails = unknown, TState = any>(tool: ToolDefinition<TParams, TDetails, TState>): void;  // 943-944
    getActiveTools(): string[]; getActiveTools(): string[];                 // 994-995
    getAllTools(): ToolInfo[]; setActiveTools(toolNames: string[]): void;   // 996-998
```
Tool *interception* is possible via `on("tool_call")` / `on("tool_result")` / `on("tool_execution_*")` (types.d.ts:937-942), but no `callTool()` exists — an extension can only call its own code, `pi.exec`, or (for the LLM) `sendUserMessage`/`sendMessage` (types.d.ts:971-983).

**(c) call a model — only through the context registry, not via `ExtensionAPI`.**
```ts
    setModel(model: Model<any>): Promise<boolean>;                          // 1005-1006
    registerProvider(provider: Provider): void;                              // 1066
    registerProvider(name: string, config: ProviderConfig): void;            // 1067
```
Actual generation uses `ExtensionContext.modelRegistry` (`types.d.ts:220-221`: `modelRegistry: ModelRegistry;`), i.e. `ModelRegistry.complete(model, context, options): Promise<AssistantMessage>` (`dist/core/model-registry.d.ts:31`), documented as *"Synchronous compatibility facade exposed to extensions"* (`dist/core/model-registry.d.ts:19`). No `pi.complete(...)` shortcut exists.

**(d) parallel / background work — nothing built in.** No timer, worker, queue, or scheduler member. The only "fire and forget" member is:
```ts
    /** Trigger compaction without awaiting completion. */
    compact(options?: CompactOptions): void;                                // types.d.ts:245-246
```
Parallelism therefore comes from plain JS (`Promise.all` in your own code) and from the harness's own tool fan-out (`docs/extensions.md:784`: "In the default parallel tool execution mode, sibling tool calls from the same assistant message are preflighted sequentially, then executed concurrently"). Per-tool opt-in/out is `ToolDefinition.executionMode?: "sequential" | "parallel"` (`types.d.ts:361-364`; declared in pi-agent-core `dist/types.d.ts:22`).

**(e) extension state shared across sessions.** Nothing session-transcending is *provided*; what exists is:
```ts
    /** Append a custom entry to the session for state persistence (not sent to LLM). */
    appendEntry<T = unknown>(customType: string, data?: T): void;           // 984-985
    events: EventBus;                                                        // 1082-1083
```
`appendEntry` writes into the *current* session file (per-session). `events` is `{ emit(channel, data); on(channel, handler) }` (`dist/core/event-bus.d.ts:1-3`) — in-process, per event-bus instance, shared between the extensions loaded into one runtime. Cross-session sharing is only whatever your module-level variables hold (see Q4 for lifetime) or what you persist yourself (Scholar: Obsidian/state files).

## 2. Subagent / agent-spawning capability reachable from an extension

**None exists in the API.** Exhaustive grep of `dist/**` for `subagent|sub-agent|spawnAgent|runTask|TaskTool` returns matches only in `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `docs/*`, and `examples/**`. There is no exported symbol to quote — the nearest exported artifact is the *example* tool registration:
```ts
	pi.registerTool({
		name: "subagent",
		label: "Subagent",            // examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:472-474
```
whose implementation spawns an OS process, not an in-process agent:
```ts
			const invocation = getPiInvocation(args);
			const proc = spawn(invocation.command, invocation.args, {   // examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:345-346
	const args: string[] = ["--mode", "json", "-p", "--no-session"];    // examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:300
```
Confirmed absent at product level too: `README.md:501` — "**No sub-agents.** There's many ways to do this. Spawn pi instances via tmux, or build your own with [extensions](#extensions), or install a package that does it your way." And the built-in tool vocabulary contains no `task`:
```ts
export type ToolName = "read" | "bash" | "powershell" | "edit" | "write" | "grep" | "find" | "ls";   // dist/core/tools/index.d.ts:20
```
(grep for `name: "task"` / `"task"` across `dist/core` and `dist/bundle` → no tool definition; the only `Task`-ish hits are unrelated Anthropic SDK strings.)

Child processes *can* be pointed at specific extensions via CLI flags: `extensions?: string[]`, `noExtensions?: boolean`, `tools?: string[]` (`dist/cli/args.d.ts:27-32`).

## 3. Concurrency limit / rate limiting / queue for model requests from an extension

**Not documented and not implemented.** The call chain is a straight passthrough with no limiter:
```js
    complete(model, context, options) {
        return this.runtime.complete(model, context, options);     // dist/core/model-registry.js:65-66
```
```js
    complete(model, context, options) {
        return this.stream(model, context, options).result();      // dist/core/model-runtime.js:458-459
```
```js
    async complete(model, context, options) {
        return this.stream(model, context, options).result();      // pi-ai dist/models.js:387-388
```
`ModelRuntime.stream` just prepares auth and calls `provider.stream(...)` (`dist/core/model-runtime.js:454-457`) — no semaphore/queue/in-flight cap anywhere on that path (greps for `concurren|semaphore|Limiter|rate.?limit|maxConcurrent` over `dist/**` and over `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/**` return only retry logic, undici pool internals, and unrelated provider strings).

The only serialization present is *credential-scoped*, not request-scoped:
```js
    /** Serialize tasks per provider id without releasing the chain before active work settles. */
    enqueue(providerId, task, options) {                            // pi-ai dist/auth/credential-store.js:10-11
```
Retry is configurable but is not a rate limit:
```ts
export interface ProviderRetrySettings {
    timeoutMs?: number;
    maxRetries?: number;              // dist/core/settings-manager.d.ts:13-16
```
Docs only warn that refresh is unbounded without a signal — `docs/extensions.md:1746`: "Public `ModelRuntime.refresh()` and `ModelRegistry.refresh()` calls accept an optional signal and are unbounded when it is omitted; extensions and applications choose their own deadlines." **Conclusion: any cap (e.g. 4-6 concurrent reviews) is the extension's own responsibility** — which is exactly what Scholar already does:
```ts
export const REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6;                                  // review-layer.ts:76
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, packets.length) }, worker));   // review-layer.ts:513
      response = await abortable(
        Promise.race([options.modelRegistry.complete(options.model, context, requestOptions), stallPromise]),   // review-runtime.ts:296-297
```

## 4. Do subagents see the same extension's tools/hooks, and share module state?

**For the only subagent mechanism the SDK provides (a child `pi` process): no — nothing is shared.** Each process discovers and loads extensions itself:
```ts
export declare function discoverAndLoadExtensions(configuredPaths: string[], cwd: string, agentDir?: string, eventBus?: EventBus): Promise<LoadExtensionsResult>;   // dist/core/extensions/loader.d.ts:22
```
A child spawned with `--mode json -p --no-session` (`examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:300`) starts its own runner, its own `ExtensionContext`, its own session file, and its own module instances; the parent's registered tools are visible to it only if they also load there, or if the parent passes an explicit allowlist (`--tools ...`, `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:307`). The README for that example states the isolation intent: "**Isolated context**: Each subagent runs in a separate `pi` process" (`examples/extensions/subagent/README.md:7`).

**In-process nuance (partially confirmed):** if an extension instead called the SDK's `createAgentSession()` itself, the nested session gets its own `LoadExtensionsResult` (`dist/core/sdk.d.ts:48-49`, `CreateAgentSessionResult.extensionsResult`), and the resource loader uses the *cached* loader (`dist/core/resource-loader.js:412,426,441`: `loadExtensionsCached(...)`). Caching is at module level keyed by extension path + resolved cwd:
```js
        const cachedFactory = extensionCache.get(extensionPath);     // dist/core/extensions/loader.js:411
        moduleCache: false,                                          // dist/core/extensions/loader.js:417
```
```js
async function initializeExtension(factory, extensionPath, resolvedPath, cwd, eventBus, runtime) {   // loader.js:458
        await factory(load.api);                                     // loader.js:462
```
[INFERENCE] Because the *module* is evaluated once per (path, cwd generation) while the *factory* is invoked once per load, two in-process sessions would get separate `Extension` objects (separate tool/handler registries) but would share module-level mutable state of the extension file. I did not find a test or doc asserting this either way, so treat the module-state-sharing half as **unconfirmed**.

**Unconfirmed / out of scope:** the *harness* here is not pi (the `task`/`agent://` tooling referenced in this session's prompt does not exist in this SDK). I grepped `C:/Users/basam/.pi/**` for `"task"` and `name: "task"` (no matches) and grepped the whole `pi-node/current/node_modules` tree for `subagent|sub-agent|spawnAgent|runTask` (matches only inside pi-coding-agent docs/CHANGELOG/examples) and the pi-server package for `subagent|spawnAgent|name: "task"|TaskTool` (no matches). Whether the actual host harness's `task` tool propagates extension tools/state to subagent sessions therefore **could not be confirmed from the installed SDK** — the evidence points to pi 0.85.1 having no such tool at all.

## 5. `ExtensionContext`: session id, subagent detection, abort plumbing

```ts
export interface ExtensionContext {                  // dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:209
    sessionManager: ReadonlySessionManager;          // 218-219
    signal: AbortSignal | undefined;                 // 235-236
    abort(): void;                                   // 237-238
    isIdle(): boolean;                               // 231-232
    hasPendingMessages(): boolean;                   // 240
```
- **Active session id: yes, indirectly** — `ReadonlySessionManager` is `Pick<SessionManager, "getCwd" | "getSessionDir" | "getSessionId" | "getSessionFile" | ...>` (`dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:140`), with `getSessionId(): string` at line 208 and `getSessionFile(): string | undefined` at 209. Same data is exported to child shells: `env.PI_SESSION_ID = ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId();` (`dist/core/tools/bash.js:128`), and the child env is scrubbed of inherited values first (`bash.js:121-125`: `delete env.PI_SESSION_ID; ...`).
- **Subagent-vs-main detection: no.** There is no `isSubagent`/`parentSession`/agent-id member on `ExtensionContext`; the closest signals are `SessionStartEvent.reason: "startup" | "reload" | "new" | "resume" | "fork"` (`types.d.ts:404-408`) and `sessionManager.getSessionFile() === undefined` for `--no-session` children. **Explicitly unconfirmed**: nothing I read establishes an API for distinguishing a subagent run from the main run.
- **Abort plumbing a long parallel operation must respect: yes.** `ctx.signal` is "The current abort signal, or undefined when the agent is not streaming" (`types.d.ts:235`), repeated in the tool execute signature `execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)` (`types.d.ts:372`). Docs are explicit: "Use `ctx.signal` for nested async work inside the handler. This lets Esc cancel model calls, `fetch()`, and other abort-aware operations started by the extension." (`docs/extensions.md:853`), and it is "usually `undefined` in idle or non-turn contexts such as session events, extension commands, and shortcuts fired while pi is idle" (`docs/extensions.md:1028-1029`). Scholar already threads it: `coordinator.loading.bindSignal(ctx.signal)` (`scholar/index.ts:141`) and `summarize`/review calls use `abortable(..., signal)` (`review-runtime.ts:296-299, 354-356`). Note the QA/test seam uses a hand-rolled registry: `new ModelRegistry({ complete: async ... })` (`tests/verify-scholar-figure-coverage.mjs:88`, `verify-scholar-learn-review.mjs:72`).

## Bottom line for the plan
- Spawning *real* subagents is not available from the SDK API; the only sanctioned route is `spawn("pi", ["--mode", "json", "-p", "--no-session", ...])` from inside the extension (as the shipped example does), which costs a cold process + re-discovery of extensions and does **not** share hooks/tools/state.
- Parallel **model** work *is* available today and already used by Scholar: `ctx.modelRegistry.complete(...)` / `provider.streamSimple(...)` fanned out through a bounded worker pool. Nothing in the SDK throttles those calls — Scholar's own `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6` is the only limit.
- Any new parallel path MUST thread `ctx.signal` (and Scholar's existing `abortable`/stall-timer pattern) and must handle `signal === undefined` in idle/command contexts.
